full_judgment:
4. The trial Court by its judgment and decree dated 14-11-2005 decreed the suit and gave saham to the plaintiff to the extent of "4.83 decimals" land. Against the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the plaintiff filed Title Appeal No. 241 of 2005 before the District Judge, Noakhali. Before the Appellate Court, defendant No. 2 prayed for saham by paying advoleram court fees. The Appellate Court by its judgment and decree dated 8-3-2001 allowed the appeal in part and gave saham to the plaintiff to the extent of "0.0625 acre" and defendant No. 2 to the extent of "0.1113/0.1365 acre." 

 5. Against the said judgment and decree of the Appellate Court, the plaintiff preferred the above mentioned civil revision before the High Court Division. In the civil revision, the plaintiff filed an application for withdrawal of the suit on the ground of formal defect. The defendant opposed the prayer by filing counter affidavit. The High Court Division by the impugned order allowed the prayer; hence this petition for leave to appeal. 

 7. We have considered the application for withdrawal of the suit and the impugned order of the High Court Division. It appears to us that the plaintiff in the application for withdrawal of the suit failed to point out the formal defect in framing the suit. The High Court Division did not also point out formal defect in framing of the suit in allowing the prayer for withdrawal of the suit. This is, by now, well settled that in a suit for partition, the plaintiff and the defendant stand on the same footing that is, both are in the category of plaintiff. Since defendant No. 2 wanted to proceed with the revision, the High Court Division was not correct in allowing the application. Mr AB Roy Chowdhury, however, has submitted that the plaintiff is in possession of his specific portion of share. Therefore, he was not at all required to file the suit for partition. So the prayer for withdrawal of the suit was rightly allowed. We find no substance in the submission of Mr AB Roy Chowdhury inasmuch as if the plaintiff is in possession in the specified portion of the suit land, the Advocate Commissioner shall surely maintain his possession if the preliminary decree giving him saham is maintained.
